content: Human Bites Medical Therapy: Vaccination 1. For adults aged 19 years and older, including pregnant women, administer a single dose of the diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccine intramuscularly (IM) at a dose of 0.5 mL. This dose is intended to replace one dose of the tetanus and diphtheria (Td) vaccine in individuals who have not previously received Tdap. 2. For pediatric patients aged 13 to 18 years who missed the 11to 12-year Tdap booster dose but have completed the recommended childhood DTP/DTaP vaccination series, administer a single dose of Tdap vaccine IM at 0.5 mL as a catch-up. 3. For pediatric patients aged 11 to 12 years who have completed the recommended childhood DTP/DTaP vaccination series but have not yet received a Tdap booster dose, administer a single dose of Tdap vaccine IM at 0.5 mL. 4. For adults aged 19 years and older who have previously received a one-time dose of Tdap, administer a single dose of the tetanus and diphtheria (Td) vaccine IM at 0.5 mL every 10 years as a booster. Dog Bites Medical Therapy: Vaccination 1. For unvaccinated patients exposed to an animal suspected of having rabies: Adults: Administer rabies immune globulin (RIG) at a dose of 20 International Units per kilogram (IU/kg) intramuscularly (IM). Infiltrate as much of the full dose as possible around the wound(s), and administer the remainder IM at a site distant from the rabies vaccine administration. Repeat the rabies vaccine on days 3, 7, 14, and 28. Pediatrics: Administer rabies immune globulin (RIG) at a dose of 20 IU/kg IM. Infiltrate as much of the full dose as possible around the wound(s), and administer the remainder IM at a site distant from the rabies vaccine administration. Repeat the rabies vaccine on days 3, 7, 14, and 28. 2. For vaccinated patients exposed to an animal suspected of having rabies: Adults: Repeat the dose 3 days later. Pediatrics: Repeat the dose 3 days later. Cat Bites, Monkey Bites, Rat Bites, Pig Bites, and Tick Bites Medical Therapy Treatment regimens for these bite types are not detailed in the provided text.
